note: App-UI documentation shots (DD-031 docs/demo parity). Unlike shots.manifest.json (mid-grey capability RENDERS), these capture the actual Feature Lab APPLICATION surface — the control/inspector rail, color-mode selector, tabs, diagnostics, and the Preview/Prepare modes — so the README/docs show the interactive product, not just pretty renders. Driven by capture-app.mjs against the running Feature Lab (tools/demo, :5199). The studio-dark chrome IS the product look. The Feature Lab starts on the opt-in Studio look (DD-032); the shots that show another look, lens or plate say so (`look`, `lens`, `plate`, `lenses`). Studio is a preset a consumer opts into: the SDK's own default look is unchanged.

shots.name: app-control-panel
shots.caption: The Feature Lab: the inspector rail (move-visibility toggles, feature-role hide, segment inspection) beside a 3DBenchy colored by feature role, with the layer/segment scrub and honest capability badges.
shots.alt: The G-code Preview Feature Lab application — a 3DBenchy colored by feature role in the viewport on the Studio look, a floating feature-role legend, camera controls, a layers/segments/time scrub strip, an inspector rail with move-visibility toggles, and capability badges (featureRoles known, feedrate known) in the status bar

shots.name: app-appearance
shots.caption: The Appearance tab: the Look selector (Studio dark and light are opt-in presets; “SDK default” is no theme) above the color-mode selector, each color mode capability-gated to what the file can prove, with the active legend.
shots.alt: The Feature Lab Appearance tab showing the Look selector set to Studio dark, with a hint that Studio is an opt-in preset, the color-by selector with feature role active, and a legend of outer wall, inner wall, infill and support colors

shots.name: app-diagnostics
shots.caption: The Diagnostics tab: capability confidence badges, parse notes (what the parser inferred, approximated or kept as metadata, grouped by code with a count), and getRenderStats(): backend (hardware vs software WebGL), GPU, geometry mode, and segment counts — honest nulls, never guesses.
shots.alt: The Feature Lab Diagnostics tab showing capability confidence badges, parse notes for a 3DBenchy (6,549 commands kept as metadata, not drawn, and 1 path whose layer was inferred), and render diagnostics — backend 3d-webgl, the GPU renderer string, geometry tubes and segment counts

shots.name: app-prepare
shots.caption: Prepare mode: interactive source-model viewing (STL / 3MF) on a 256 mm build plate, with the honest materials tier, the object/placement counts and the plate-placement line (tier and offset exactly as the viewer reports them).
shots.alt: The Feature Lab in Prepare mode showing a colored 3MF source model on a build plate under the Studio look, with a Source Model panel reporting 3 objects, 3 placements and materials known, and a Build Plate panel with a placement line

shots.name: app-studio-light
shots.caption: The Studio light look on the same 3DBenchy: opt in with `theme: studioTheme('light')` and `cameraFov: STUDIO_CAMERA_FOV`. Without a theme the SDK renders its default look.
shots.alt: The Feature Lab with the Look selector set to Studio light: a 3DBenchy colored by feature role on a pale grey gradient backdrop above a mid-grey build plate with a white-and-dark grid and a soft contact shadow

shots.name: app-lens-compare
shots.caption: The same 3DBenchy at the SDK default 50° lens (left) and the Studio preset's 32° lens (right): a longer lens flattens perspective, and the framing is lens-aware so the model stays fully in view at both.
shots.alt: Two renders of the same 3DBenchy side by side, labelled 50 degrees (SDK default lens) and 32 degrees (Studio lens); the 32 degree render shows less perspective distortion, and the model fits the frame in both

shots.name: app-prepare-plate
shots.caption: Plate selection on a SYNTHETIC two-plate 3MF (generated for the demo, not a slicer export): plate 2 is selected through render scope, and the placement line reads `inferred` with the one-workspace-cell offset the viewer subtracted to draw it on the bed.
shots.alt: The Feature Lab in Prepare mode showing one block on a build plate, the plate selector set to the second synthetic plate, and the placement line reading inferred with an x offset of minus 307.2 millimetres

shots.name: app-cnc-cut-framing
shots.caption: A CNC file with no printing moves on the Studio look: the plate is drawn see-through so the cut shows through it, there is no contact-shadow blob, and the camera centres on the work instead of the bed. Cuts have their own Cut moves toggle, so they show with Travel moves off.
shots.alt: The Feature Lab showing an Easel CNC carve of the letters CKC as pale blue lines seen through a translucent plate, with the inspector rail on the right
